title: Checkpoint: Science and Math
objective: After this level you can explain how Greek thinkers used reason to study nature.
summary: Greek thinkers studied nature through proof, measurement and argument, looking for natural causes. Archimedes prized a proof enough to want it on his grave.

cards.headline: Chapter 7 finale: Archimedes built war machines. His tomb showed geometry.
cards.body: That choice says a lot about how Greek thinkers ranked their work, and how they went about studying nature.

cards.headline: A sphere in a cylinder
cards.body: Archimedes proved that a sphere has two-thirds the volume of the cylinder that just holds it, and he asked for a sphere in a cylinder on his tomb. About a century and a half later, Cicero found it, overgrown with plants. According to Plutarch, Archimedes thought so little of practical inventions that he wrote nothing about them. The proof, not the machine, was the prize.

cards.headline: Three ways to reason about nature

items.label: Proof
points: Euclid proved geometry from stated starting points
Archimedes worked out the law of the lever

items.label: Measurement
points: Eratosthenes turned a 7° angle into Earth’s size
Hipparchus compared star positions across centuries

items.label: Argument
points: Hippocratic writers sought natural causes of disease
Democritus argued for atoms no one could see

cards.headline: One story
cards.body: Put Chapter 7 together. Greek thinkers looked for natural causes, not divine ones, and trusted reasoning that could be checked: a proof, a measured angle, a star position in an old record. They got plenty wrong, from a drum-shaped Earth to the four humors. But checking was built in. Comparing old records is exactly how Hipparchus found the stars slowly drifting.

questions.prompt: Science and Math recap: how does Euclid’s Elements establish its results?

options.label: By measuring real fields and buildings
By collecting the opinions of experts
By proving them step by step from stated starting points
By testing them with water and weights

questions.explanation: The Elements proves each result from its definitions, postulates and common notions.

questions.prompt: Science and Math recap: what did the Antikythera mechanism’s pointers show?

options.label: The Sun and Moon in the zodiac, and eclipses to come
The time of day in every Greek city
The depth of the sea below the ship
The weight of gold in a wreath

questions.explanation: Turned by a crank, its gears showed the Sun and Moon in the zodiac, the Moon’s phases and coming eclipses.

questions.prompt: Science and Math recap: whose big idea rested on argument about something no one could observe?

options.label: Eratosthenes’ size of the Earth
Hipparchus’s drifting stars
